title: Petra and the Wreck
premise: Salvage diver Ulyana Halloran recovers a sealed chest from a river wreck the navy refuses to acknowledge, and inside finds letters proving her long-lost brother survived a border war he was officially killed in. Pursued by naval intelligence officer Petra Voss, who is ordered to bury the chest and everyone who touched it, Ulyana flees into the mountains with the only witness, a defector cartographer named Ilya. As snows close the passes, duty and conscience war within Petra, who has begun to question what she is protecting. In the end, Petra lets them cross, delivering the letters herself to a newspaper at terrible personal cost, while Ulyana finally learns where her brother's story ended — and that belonging sometimes means choosing strangers over country.
about_author: Quentin Sandoval is the pen name of a former merchant marine who spent a decade diving wrecks in cold northern rivers before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about people caught between institutions and their own hearts.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Diving a classified wreck site, she raises a chest stamped with a vanished nation's seal and hides it before the navy can log it. Inside are letters in her dead brother's handwriting, dated years after his official death. The emotional beat is vertigo: grief overturned by hope, and the first flicker of fear as she realizes someone on shore watched her find it.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ulyana and Petra Voss, the intelligence officer sent to recover the chest quietly. Ulyana tracks down Ilya, the last man who might read the letters; Petra closes the net, burning bridges behind her. The beat is pursuit becoming personal — Petra reads one letter against orders and cannot un-know what it says.

chapters.title: Ahead of the Snows
chapters.summary: Ulyana, Ilya, and Petra — now openly hunting them — race up the mountain passes as the first storm hits. An avalanche separates Petra from her team, and Ulyana saves her life against every instinct. The climax arrives when Petra, half-frozen, must choose: radio her superiors or lie for the first time in her career. She lies.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The three descend together, forging an uneasy alliance, and deliver the letters to a journalist before Petra surrenders to face court-martial. Ulyana learns her brother lived out his days as a village schoolteacher across the border — loved, ordinary, gone. The resolution is bittersweet: justice incomplete, but Ulyana no longer alone, and Petra discovering that duty, rightly understood, can mean mercy.
